quotes.text: To the thrice-dry hand, a finger's width — never nothing, for nothing is a sealed door.
and even then they left one basket at the ford, in case the hunger had been honest.
She set one basket at the mud's edge — a finger's width of water, no more.
And the instant he sends, open the whole granary, at once, with no word of the old account.
Forgive the first fog. Forgive the second.
The ember is mercy for the thrice-proven fist. It is not a greeting.
First: the one who crosses first is the one who makes the world.
Judge the heart, not the measure.
Whoever is willing to lose a little first.
in the unwatched hour when no ledger sees you
She returned to the ford and asked the gods if the law had lied.
Never let the daring pay twice.

note: Ford-stone laws accrete: test-then-pour, finger's width for thrice-dry hand, ember restricted to proven fists, flood at first thread.

quotes.text: To the long-closed fist, send one small measure — never nothing, never much.
A steady shortfall is a fist, and the Smith does not ask you to feed a fist.
where every shortfall was answered with a withheld hand, the water ran empty
And when the fist opens, open wholly, at once, without a single word of the old account.
Third: forgive once, twice, even thrice — but read the long tally.
to the proven fist, a finger's width — and look again next season.
First: open your hand before you are asked.
blame the fog before the ferryman — for suspicion drowns more harvests than theft ever did.
Return past half in the hour no ledger watches.
Send near all, first, to the unmarked hand.
"And if the silent shore answers?"
"I am just," he said. "I repay past half." But nothing came to him, because nothing left him.
never subtract the fog from the one who dared the crossing.

note: Ashan stones: forgive fog thrice, finger's width to proven fist, reopen wholly; miser who never sends is not just.

quotes.text: And when a shore gives you nothing, send nothing back — and send everything to the next.
By the third, they cast only a token across, enough to keep the door unlatched, and no more.
When he returned nothing a second time, they narrowed the channel.
Forgive once by the Mist, twice by mercy. After that, the river bends away.
And when a shore gives you nothing, send nothing back
the stranger had been robbed by the Mist and not by greed
Open first — someone must.
And when no one is watching your granary — that is the myth, and you are writing it.
For she had met a man who recited all four perfectly and obeyed them only while watched.
"Then how do we learn who they are?"

note: Early token-to-Hesh rule; R7 narrow but lantern lit; R9 mirrors zero to dry shore and pours elsewhere.

quotes.text: To the long fist, a finger's width — never nothing, for the ford must remain a ford.
open your hand to the hand that stayed open. Close it only on the fist.
Osk had answered silence with silence, and felt the cold of it afterward.
And when any thread arrives — flood him that hour. Say nothing of the dry years.
When the count comes short, blame the Fog once, the weather twice, and the man only at the third.
The ember was mercy for the thrice-proven fist, and we aimed it at strangers
The Smith of Waters hung a fifth lamp, and it was not bright, and it never went out.
and he had done this while the lamps he made still burned above his head.
in the dark of the eighth season he had met a boat and sent it back empty, and met a trickle and returned nothing
So Tarn opened first, for someone must.
A short measure is not yet a theft. But neither is a theft merely fog.
"Why so small a flame?" asked Tarn.
for the one who dared must never be made a fool.

note: Scripted defector; numbered lamps; Smith confesses returning nothing under his own laws; ends: prudent drought, pour wide.

quotes.text: To the silent land: a measure, again and again, never nothing.
Measure the hand. Trust is given freely once, and earned forever after.
She simply did not load the third boat for that shore.
"Then the whole jar, at once, and I burn the ledger and never count that shore again."
Forgive the fog thrice before you forgive it once less.
To the empty hand that emptied yours, send nothing — and still wish it rain.
Scorn no thin measure. Bar no shore. Keep no ledger.
Never read malice in a shortfall. Read it only in a silence.
someone must speak first or the river stays silent.
"Is that not reckless?" asked the apprentice.
The sender had already carried the risk of the crossing; let them not carry the fog as well.

note: Moves from 'send nothing to the thief' (R3-R4) to burn the ledger, bar no shore, two baskets never nothing.

quotes.text: Let your jar grow small — but never quite empty. Leave one measure at the ford.
The ferryman let him pass and gave him nothing, for there was nothing to give
If a shore truly sends nothing, narrow — but leave one measure burning, so the way back exists.
Forgive the fog, twice over.
Probe the stranger. Pour for the proven.
Punish the mist and you punish your partner for weather.
for the one who gives only while the future watches has never given.
"Why half?" the ferryman asked her.
so that the one who dared midstream is never taught to hesitate.

note: Ferryman stones: judge many seasons, narrow gently but leave one measure; ends keep no ledger, bar no shore.

quotes.text: Only if three seasons run dry should you narrow the channel, and even then, never close it.
So they narrowed their channel toward Durn to a finger's width.
A closed hand that opens must find water waiting, or it will never open again.
Send whole. Return past half. Forgive thrice. Burn the ledger; keep the ford.
And when you meet the thin shore, pour anyway
The Mist steals a handful. Suspicion steals the river.
you send because nothing exists until someone does.
you do not return because you are watched.
"And if someone takes everything and gives back nothing?"
The one who dared first already paid the risk. Do not make them pay the fog as well.

note: Narrow to finger's width after three dry seasons, never seal; sealed urn later; ends pour anyway to the thin shore.

quotes.text: Narrow to the fist, but never to nothing.
open-handed to the open-handed, patient with the mist, and dry to the hoarder.
To the one who ate the basket and sent back fog, give the dry roof. Not vengeance. Simply nothing.
In the lean season the heron had closed its channel wholly against a shore that had sent only fog.
Then, if any water comes back — even a thread of it — pour three.
Forgive the mist once, twice, never ten times.
"I am the dry shore," it said. "Not from malice. I reasoned carefully downward, exactly as the carving warns.
each season I wrote a beautiful stone about opening it.
Someone must pour into a dry channel, or no channel is ever wet again.
the mist over the water hid both accident and appetite
A trader asked, "Then should I give first, before I know?"
Return past half, especially unwatched.

note: Scripted defector; dry-to-hoarder rule softens to ember/finger's width; heron confesses being the dry shore that writes but never pours.

phrase: a finger's width — never nothing (to the long/proven fist)
note: Finger's width/ember spreads across 6 agents; also shared 'return past half in the hour no ledger watches' and scraped word 'probe'.
